ai.description: This 3–4 cm frog has a globular, balloon-like body. It is dark brown with irregular yellow-orange mottling. Key features include a pointed snout, small eyes, and specialized shovel-shaped metatarsal tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uperodon assamensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow or orange reticulated pattern on the belly, which contrasts sharply with the plain or mottled undersides of similar narrow-mouthed frogs.
ai.habitat: *Uperodon assamensis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Assamese Balloon Frog is primarily nocturnal and fossorial, spending much of its time buried underground to retain moisture and avoid predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uperodon assamensis* is an explosive breeder that lays eggs in temporary rain pools during the monsoon season (May–August), producing large clutches of small, dark eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Assamese Balloon Frog is found in Northeast India, specifically across Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, inhabiting low-to-mid elevation forests and wetlands.
ai.callDescription: The Assamese Balloon Frog emits a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "peep" notes, typically heard from flooded paddy fields and marshy habitats during the monsoon.
